extracted.intended_audience: EPO examiners acting as ISA/IPEA and international patent applicants/representatives
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance on how the EPO (as ISA/IPEA) should examine international (PCT) applications, covering claim clarity/conciseness/support, unity, priority, patentability exclusions, industrial applicability, prior art and related procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conciseness, number of claims
rubrics_metrics.description: Where it is found that the claims lack conciseness under Art. 6, it may be appropriate for the examiner to first invite the applicant to provide informal clarification before the search is carried out.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See ISPE Guidelines 5.42; EPO applies option GL/ISPE A5.42. If independent claims of the same category result in lack of clarity and conciseness (see GL/PCT‑EPO F‑IV, 3.2), an objection may arise under Rule 6.

rubrics_metrics.name: Support in the description
rubrics_metrics.description: Claims must be supported by the description; dependent claims must find adequate support in the disclosure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See ISPE Guidelines 5.43. If claims lack support under Art. 6, examiner may invite informal clarification before search (GL/PCT‑EPO B‑VIII, 3.3–3.6). The examiner applies the same criteria as in EPO Guidelines (mutatis mutandis).

rubrics_metrics.name: Extent of generalisation in claims
rubrics_metrics.description: An invention that opens up a whole new field is entitled to more generality in the claims than one concerned with advances in a known technology.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See ISPE Guidelines 5.52; evaluate generality in light of the invention's technical contribution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Objection of lack of support (Art. 6)
rubrics_metrics.description: If a broad claim is not supported over its whole breadth, the onus of demonstrating full support lies with the applicant once examiner sets out a reasoned case.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See GL/PCT‑EPO F‑IV, 6.3 and ISPE Guidelines 5.53. Examiner should set out reasons; applicant must show support or provide amendments/arguments. Informal clarification may be sought before search.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lack of support vs insufficient disclosure
rubrics_metrics.description: An objection of lack of support under Art. 6 can also amount to insufficient disclosure under Art. 5 when the disclosure does not enable the skilled person to carry out the invention across the claimed breadth.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Both requirements reflect that claim terms should be commensurate with the invention's technical contribution. Example: essential technical features highlighted in the description must be in independent claim(s), otherwise both Art. 5 and Art. 6 objections may be justified.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition in terms of function
rubrics_metrics.description: Claims defined in functional terms must be assessed for support and sufficiency.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See ISPE Guidelines 5.56 and GL/PCT‑EPO F‑IV, 2.1 and 4.10 for how functional definitions affect support/clarity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Support for dependent claims
rubrics_metrics.description: Dependent claims must be supported by the description according to the same criteria as applied in EPO examination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See GL/PCT‑EPO F‑IV, 6.6 and ISPE guidance referenced for specifics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evaluation of essential features
rubrics_metrics.description: Use examples in the EPO Guidelines Annex to determine whether a claim contains all essential features of the invention; same criteria apply under PCT.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The examiner applies the Annex examples mutatis mutandis when assessing essential features under the PCT.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unity of invention (one general inventive concept)
rubrics_metrics.description: The international application must relate to one invention only or to a group of inventions so linked as to form a single general inventive concept.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See Art. 17(3)(a) and Rule 13.1. Lack of clarity of claims alone is not sufficient for lack of unity. Claims in different categories or multiple independent claims are not per se lack of unity if substantive criteria (Rules 13.1–13.3) are met.

rubrics_metrics.name: Impact of claim sequence on unity
rubrics_metrics.description: Normally sequence of claims should not impact unity determination, but it affects which invention is considered the 'first invention' mentioned in the claims.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See GL/PCT‑EPO F‑V, 8.2; the identified 'first invention' influences search/examination scope.

rubrics_metrics.name: Special technical features
rubrics_metrics.description: Identification of special technical features is part of unity assessment and search practice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See ISPE Guidelines 10.01 and 10.12–10.16 and Rule 13.2 for determining features that link claimed inventions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Alternatives (multiple claimed options)
rubrics_metrics.description: Alternatives in claims must be examined for unity and may be handled according to ISPE Guidelines on alternatives.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See ISPE Guidelines 10.09; presence of non‑novel alternatives can indicate lack of unity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Markush grouping and unity
rubrics_metrics.description: For Markush claims, a 'significant structural element' need not be novel per se but must distinguish claimed compounds in relation to the common property/activity; if at least one alternative is not novel, unity should be reconsidered.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See ISPE Guidelines 10.17. If a compound within the Markush group is known in combination with the property, that may indicate lack of unity for the remaining alternatives.

rubrics_metrics.name: Individual features in a claim
rubrics_metrics.description: Individual claim features must be considered in unity assessment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See ISPE Guidelines 10.10 and GL/PCT‑EPO G‑VII, 7.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lack of unity 'a priori' or 'a posteriori'
rubrics_metrics.description: Determine whether lack of unity exists from the outset ('a priori') or arises after considering prior art ('a posteriori').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See ISPE Guidelines 10.03 for distinctions and handling.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examiner's approach to unity
rubrics_metrics.description: Follow ISPE Guidelines for the examiner's approach to unity determinations, including reasoning and communication.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See ISPE Guidelines 10.04 and GL/PCT‑EPO references; when lack of unity is found, subject‑matter is divided among separate inventions and search/examination actions follow accordingly (e.g., inviting payment of additional search fees).

rubrics_metrics.name: Reasoning for a lack of unity objection
rubrics_metrics.description: Examiners must set out reasoned case when objecting for lack of unity (apply EPO Guidelines mutatis mutandis).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See GL/PCT‑EPO F‑V, 8.1; provide clear reasoning to justify lack of unity finding.

rubrics_metrics.name: Determination of the invention first mentioned in the claims
rubrics_metrics.description: Rules for deciding which invention is 'first mentioned' in the claims are applied as in the EPO Guidelines.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See GL/PCT‑EPO F‑V, 8.2 and GL/PCT‑EPO B‑VII, 2.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dependent claims and unity
rubrics_metrics.description: Consideration of dependent claims in relation to unity follows ISPE Guidelines 10.06–10.08.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Dependent claims may affect unity and search scope; see referenced ISPE provisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lack of unity during search (invitation to pay additional search fees)
rubrics_metrics.description: If lack of unity is noted at search stage, a search is conducted for the invention first mentioned and the applicant is invited to pay additional search fees (Form PCT/ISA/206) for other inventions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See GL/PCT‑EPO B‑VII, 2 and ISPE Guidelines 10.60. Rules 6.4 and 13.4 and Rule 40.1(i) are relevant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lack of unity during PCT Chapter II procedure (additional fees for examination)
rubrics_metrics.description: If additional search fees were paid in Chapter I and the objection was partly upheld, the applicant will normally be invited (Form 405) to pay additional preliminary examination fees in Chapter II to have searched inventions examined.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Inventions for which no search fees were paid cannot be pursued and will not be objected to or commented on. See GL/PCT‑EPO C‑V and ISPE Guidelines 10.71–10.73.

rubrics_metrics.name: Right to priority
rubrics_metrics.description: Rules governing the right to priority for the WO‑ISA and effect of claiming priority are set out (priority must refer to an earlier application).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See GL/PCT‑EPO B‑XI, 4; Art. 8(1), Rules 2.4, 17.1. Priority date becomes the effective date for international examination (written opinion and IPER); international filing date remains relevant for search.

rubrics_metrics.name: Filing date as effective date
rubrics_metrics.description: For certain purposes the international filing date is used as the effective date (e.g., for international search).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See ISPE Guidelines 6.01 and relevant PCT rules; note distinctions between filing date and priority date.

rubrics_metrics.name: Priority date as effective date
rubrics_metrics.description: When an international application claims priority, the priority date (filing date of earlier application) is used to calculate certain time limits and for international examination purposes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See Art. 11, 14 and Rule 20; priority must be to an earlier application (at least one day earlier as per Rule 2.4 and Article 4C(2) Paris Convention).

rubrics_metrics.name: Validly claiming priority / Claiming priority formalities
rubrics_metrics.description: Requirements and formalities for validly claiming priority, including declarations, certified copies and translations of previous applications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See ISPE Guidelines 6.03, 6.11–6.17 and Euro‑PCT Guide points 141/144 for certified copies. Details on declaration of priority and translation obligations are provided.

rubrics_metrics.name: Subsequent application considered as first application (limitations)
rubrics_metrics.description: Some applications cannot be recognised as a 'first application' for priority purposes (e.g., US continuation or continuation‑in‑part where subject‑matter was already disclosed in original US application).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples include US 'con' and 'cip' forms and national applications claiming priority from national utility models; specific formal statements and declarations are required in US con/cip cases. See ISPE Guidelines 6.04.

rubrics_metrics.name: Multiple priorities
rubrics_metrics.description: Rules and guidance on claiming multiple priorities to different earlier applications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See ISPE Guidelines 6.05 for handling multiple priority claims and their effects on effective dates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Determining priority dates / Examining validity of a right to priority
rubrics_metrics.description: Examination of whether a claimed priority is valid and whether the same invention is present between filings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See ISPE Guidelines 6.06–6.09 for tests on identity of invention and GL/PCT‑EPO references regarding disclaimers and their effect on identity of invention under Art. 8.

rubrics_metrics.name: Priority claim not valid (consequences)
rubrics_metrics.description: Guidance on situations where a priority claim is not valid and consequences for effective dates.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See ISPE Guidelines 6.10; examiner may remark where filing date exceeds priority year and record days exceeded in WO‑ISA.

rubrics_metrics.name: Withdrawal, correction, addition of priority claims
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicant may withdraw a priority claim up to 30 months from the priority date; correction or addition is governed by ISPE provisions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See Art. 11, Rule 4.10 and ISPE Guidelines 6.11, 6.16, 8.10 for correction/addition; withdrawal rules and timing are specified.

rubrics_metrics.name: Re‑establishment / Restoration of priority rights
rubrics_metrics.description: An applicant may request restoration of priority rights up to two months after expiry of the priority year; restoration criteria differ ('due care' vs 'unintentional') depending on receiving Office and EPO recognition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See Rule 26bis.3. EPO as receiving/designated Office uses 'due care' criterion; if restored under 'unintentional' by receiving Office, a new request may be needed at EPO. Examiner may notify applicant and set time limits if doubts exist.

rubrics_metrics.name: Objective of international preliminary examination (patentability questions)
rubrics_metrics.description: International preliminary examination aims to formulate a preliminary and non‑binding opinion on novelty, inventive step and industrial applicability of the claimed invention.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See Art. 33(1) and Rule 43bis.1(a). The PCT procedure is to provide an opinion, not to grant patents.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examination practice for excluded subject‑matter
rubrics_metrics.description: Exclusions from patentability apply only to the extent the application relates to excluded subject‑matter as such; the claim must be considered as a whole to decide technical character.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See GL/PCT‑EPO G‑II and ISPE Guidelines 9.02–9.15; the EPO's discretion under Agreement with WIPO determines search/examination on excluded matter.

rubrics_metrics.name: List of exclusions (discoveries, scientific theories, mathematical theories, aesthetic creations, schemes/rules/methods of business, programs for computers, presentations of information)
rubrics_metrics.description: Certain categories (discoveries, scientific theories, mathematical methods, aesthetic creations, business methods, pure mental acts, computer programs, presentations of information) are listed as subject‑matter the ISA/IPEA is not required to search or examine.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See Rules 39 and 67 and ISPE Guidelines 9.02–9.15. EPO may exercise discretion to exclude matter falling under Art. 52(2)/(3) EPC when acting as ISA/IPEA.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exclusions from and limitation of international preliminary examination (ordre public/morality)
rubrics_metrics.description: PCT does not explicitly define ordre public/morality, but Rule 9 prohibits expressions contrary thereto; EPO may exclude such matter from search/examination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See Rule 9 and GL/PCT‑EPO G‑II, 4.1; EPO discretion applies mutatis mutandis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Surgery, therapy and diagnostic methods
rubrics_metrics.description: Such methods may be excluded (Art. 53(c) EPC) and generally no search/preliminary examination is carried out by EPO as ISA/IPEA on these topics.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See ISPE Guidelines 9.08–9.10 and GL/PCT‑EPO G‑II, 4.2.

rubrics_metrics.name: Biotechnological inventions and exceptions
rubrics_metrics.description: Biotechnological inventions (products containing biological material or processes involving biological material) are subject to exclusions/discretion under Art. 53(b) EPC and may not be searched/examined as ISA/IPEA.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See ISPE Guidelines 9.06 and GL/PCT‑EPO G‑II, 5.2–5.5; EPO applies discretion and EPO Guidelines apply mutatis mutandis when application enters regional phase.

rubrics_metrics.name: Industrial applicability
rubrics_metrics.description: Industrial applicability must be assessed; the international preliminary examination formulates a preliminary opinion on this requirement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See ISPE Guidelines 14.01–14.06 and Art. 33(4). Methodology guidance in ISPE is referenced.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prior art — general definition and scope
rubrics_metrics.description: Prior art consists of everything made available to the public anywhere in the world by written disclosure (including drawings) capable of assisting determination of novelty/inventive step if made available before the international filing date (or priority date where validly claimed).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See Art. 33(2), Rules 33.1 and 64.1 and ISPE Guidelines 11.01 and 11.12. No geographic or language restrictions; no age limit on prior art documents.

rubrics_metrics.name: Enabling disclosures (prior art)
rubrics_metrics.description: The principles for determining whether prior documents are enabling and thus anticipate claimed subject matter follow EPO Guidelines mutatis mutandis.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See GL/PCT‑EPO G‑IV, 2 and ISPE guidance for enabling disclosure tests.

rubrics_metrics.name: Date of filing or priority date as effective date for novelty
rubrics_metrics.description: For international preliminary examination, prior art is considered if publicly available before the international filing date or, where priority is validly claimed, before the priority date; different claims/alternatives may have different effective dates.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See Rule 64.1(a),(b), GL/ISPE 11.24–11.26, and GL/PCT‑EPO references on effective dates and consequences of furnishing missing parts under Rule 20.5.

rubrics_metrics.name: Documents in a non‑official language of the (S)ISA or IPEA
rubrics_metrics.description: If applicant disputes relevance of a document in a non‑official language cited at search, examiner should consider applicant's reasons and may obtain a translation (or relevant part) and send it to the applicant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See GL/PCT‑EPO B‑X, 9.1.2–9.1.3; if examiner still finds document relevant, send translation with next communication in PCT Chapter II phase.

rubrics_metrics.name: Machine translations as evidence
rubrics_metrics.description: Examiners may rely on machine translations to overcome language barriers and should send such translation to the applicant; machine translations that render meaning are acceptable unless applicant adduces evidence of defects.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mere grammatical/syntactic errors that do not affect understanding do not prevent qualification as a translation. A general statement that machine translations cannot be trusted is insufficient to contest their value; applicant bears burden to produce improved translation showing defects.
